newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds softer with U.S. mkt, slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds softer with U.S. mkt, slow trade.

text.p: Argentine bonds were flat to lower late morning Monday as the market got off to a sluggish start to the week.
Early price gains in London were reversed with declines in U.S. Treasuries as the U.S. market was pulled lower with the dollar.
"The market is weakening a little from earlier levels," said a trader at a local bank.
Argentina's FRB due 2005 was flat at 91-1/2, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 was untraded so far in the session. It closed at 126.60 on Friday.
Traders said activity was very slim as investors stayed on the sidelines, awaiting an opportunity to enter the market at levels which were seen attractive.
"The market is sustained at these levels," said another trader.
Separately, traders said the pricing of an Argentine seven-year 1.5 billion mark bond at 195 basis points over similarly dated Bunds was a good signal for the market.
"The government is continuing to seek cheap financing," said the first trader.
